title: Comparative genomic analysis of Artemisia argyi reveals asymmetric expansion of terpene synthases and conservation of artemisinin biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: A. argyi comparative TPS/ADS genomics and artemisinin-pathway conservation
decision_rationale: Primary comparative-genomics study directly informs the evolution section; assembly, haplotype, annotation, and recombinant-function boundaries prevent treating reported copy counts as settled orthology or native pathway flux.

title: In vitro activity and selectivity of Artemisia afra and Artemisia annua aqueous extracts against artemisinin-resistant Plasmodium falciparum.
evidence_scope: comparative aqueous-extract activity against resistant P. falciparum
decision_rationale: Primary resistant-parasite/selectivity study strengthens the malaria evidence stream; aqueous matrix effects and species-specific chemistry do not establish a terpene mechanism or clinical efficacy.

title: Discovery and modulation of diterpenoid metabolism improves glandular trichome formation, artemisinin production and stress resilience in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: A. annua diterpene-synthase diversity, trichome formation, artemisinin, and stress resilience

title: The reference genome sequence of Artemisia argyi provides insights into secondary metabolism biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: A. argyi reference genome, MeJA response, and terpenoid-pathway resource
decision_rationale: Primary genome/transcriptome study informs assembly-aware comparative genomics and regulatory candidate prioritization; gene-model expansion is not proof of terpene function or antiparasitic activity.

title: Comparison of phytochemical properties and expressional profiling of artemisinin synthesis-related genes in various Artemisia species.
evidence_scope: controlled five-species chemistry and pathway-gene expression
decision_rationale: Primary common-environment comparison informs species-specific chemotypes and expression limits; GC-MS assignments and correlations do not establish evolutionary gain/loss or therapeutic equivalence.

title: Efficient biosynthesis of beta-caryophyllene in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by beta-caryophyllene synthase from Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: A. argyi beta-caryophyllene synthases and engineered yeast production
decision_rationale: Primary enzyme and metabolic-engineering study informs TPS function and production feasibility; fermentation output is not in-planta abundance or antiparasitic evidence.

title: Engineering Nootkatone Biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: A. annua valencene synthase/oxidase engineering and plastid targeting
decision_rationale: Primary metabolic-engineering study informs sesquiterpene pathway design and compartment effects; engineered production does not establish native nootkatone biology or parasite activity.

title: Biotechnological Approaches for Production of Artemisinin, an Anti-Malarial Drug from Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: A. annua artemisinin tissue culture, elicitation, and metabolic engineering review
decision_rationale: Relevant review context for malaria-focused biosynthesis and production; primary enzyme, pathway, pharmacology, and clinical evidence remain separately coded.

title: Artemyrianosins A-J, cytotoxic germacrane-type sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia myriantha.
evidence_scope: A. myriantha germacrane-type sesquiterpene lactone isolation and structure
decision_rationale: Primary isolation study expands structurally confirmed STL diversity; hepatoma cytotoxicity is not antiparasitic evidence or host-selectivity evidence.

title: Artemisia annua L.: a source of novel antimalarial drugs.
evidence_scope: artemisinin chemistry biosynthesis pharmacology safety
decision_rationale: Relevant historical review; use for discovery and pathway context, not as a substitute for primary studies.

title: Antiprotozoal Effect of Artemisia indica Extracts and Essential Oil.
evidence_scope: terpene chemistry and protozoan assays
decision_rationale: Reports oil composition, multiple extract preparations, parasite-panel activity, and mammalian cytotoxicity.

title: Biosynthesis of anti-leishmanial natural products in callus cultures of Artemisia scoparia.
evidence_scope: callus chemistry and Leishmania tropica assay

title: [Research advances of biosynthesis, in vivo analysis and pharmacokinetics of chemical constituents in Artemisiae Annuae Herba].
evidence_scope: A. annua constituent biosynthesis pharmacokinetics

title: Cloning and molecular analysis of two new sesquiterpene cyclases from Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: sesquiterpene-cyclase gene family and tissue expression

title: Amorpha-4,11-diene synthase: cloning and functional expression of a key enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway of the novel antimalarial drug artemisinin.
evidence_scope: ADS enzyme function
decision_rationale: Recombinant enzyme and heterologous expression directly anchor an artemisinin-pathway step.

title: Artemisinin Related Sesquiterpenes and Essential Oil in Artemisia annua During a Vegetation Period in Vietnam.
evidence_scope: developmental chemistry and essential-oil composition
decision_rationale: Leaf, flower, fruit, stage, and oil measurements directly address tissue and phenology.

title: The genetic map of Artemisia annua L. identifies loci affecting yield of the antimalarial drug artemisinin.
evidence_scope: artemisinin-yield QTL and breeding genomics
decision_rationale: Primary linkage/QTL study connecting genetic variation with artemisinin yield; relevant to genotype–chemotype evolution, but not a cross-species orthology result.

title: Effect of sugars on artemisinin production in Artemisia annua L.: transcription and metabolite measurements.
evidence_scope: carbon-regulated artemisinin pathway expression and metabolites

title: Root regulation of artemisinin production in Artemisia annua: trichome and metabolite evidence.
evidence_scope: root–shoot regulation of glandular-trichome chemistry

title: Effect of leaf digestion and artemisinin solubility for use in oral consumption of dried Artemisia annua leaves to treat malaria.
evidence_scope: preparation and bioaccessibility of dried-leaf artemisinin

title: [Sesquiterpenoids from aerial parts of Artemisia myriantha].
evidence_scope: sesquiterpene and sesquiterpene-lactone isolation

title: Two new guaiane sesquiterpene lactones from the aerial parts of Artemisia vulgaris.
evidence_scope: guaiane sesquiterpene-lactone isolation

title: [Molecular mechanism of artemisinin biosynthesis and regulation in Artemisia annua].

title: Sesquiterpene lactones from the endemic Cape Verdean Artemisia gorgonum.

title: Comparison of antimalarial activity of Artemisia turanica extract with current drugs in vivo.

title: A phylogenetic road map to antimalarial Artemisia species.

title: Functional genomics and the biosynthesis of artemisinin.

title: Localization of enzymes of artemisinin biosynthesis to the apical cells of glandular secretory trichomes of Artemisia annua L.

evidence_scope: glandular-trichome transcriptome

title: Artemisinin biosynthesis in growing plants of Artemisia annua. A 13CO2 study.
evidence_scope: in-planta isotope tracing

title: Drying affects artemisinin dihydroartemisinic acid artemisinic acid and the antioxidant capacity of Artemisia annua L. leaves.

decision_rationale: Primary transcriptomic and targeted-metabolite study expands regulatory candidates beyond A. annua; candidate correlations require functional validation.

title: Phytochemical analysis and anti-microbial activities of Artemisia spp. and rapid isolation methods of artemisinin.
evidence_scope: comparative Ethiopian Artemisia chemistry and artemisinin isolation
decision_rationale: Primary comparative phytochemistry study adds species and extraction context; antimicrobial endpoints are not antiparasitic and crude-extract attribution remains limited.

title: Repellency and insecticidal activity of seven Mugwort (Artemisia argyi) essential oils against the malaria vector Anopheles sinensis.
evidence_scope: seven-population A. argyi oil chemotypes and malaria-vector assays
decision_rationale: Primary geographic comparison directly informs chemotype variation and vector phenotypes; oil activity remains mixture-level and requires non-target testing.

title: The transcription factors TLR1 and TLR2 negatively regulate trichome density and artemisinin levels in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: negative control of glandular trichomes and artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary loss- and gain-of-function study informs developmental regulation of a sesquiterpene lactone; it is not comparative evidence across Artemisia species.

title: Integrated metabolite profiling and transcriptome analysis reveals tissue-specific regulation of terpenoid biosynthesis in Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: A. argyi tissue-specific terpenoid metabolomics and transcriptomics
decision_rationale: Primary integrated study directly informs root, stem, and leaf variation; associations require enzyme, orthology, and specimen-level validation.

title: The truncated AaActin1 promoter is a candidate tool for metabolic engineering of artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: promoter performance in A. annua glandular secretory trichomes
decision_rationale: Primary promoter-engineering study informs compartment-targeted expression; construct performance is not evidence for natural regulatory evolution.

title: AabHLH112, a bHLH transcription factor, positively regulates sesquiterpenes biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: bHLH regulation of beta-caryophyllene epi-cedrol and beta-farnesene
decision_rationale: Primary transgenic and expression study broadens non-artemisinin sesquiterpene regulation; product and tissue effects remain A. annua-specific.

title: Full-Length Transcriptomic Sequencing and Temporal Transcriptome Expression Profiling Analyses Offer Insights into Terpenoid Biosynthesis in Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: temporal and full-length A. argyi terpenoid transcriptomics
decision_rationale: Primary temporal transcriptome and volatile-profile study informs harvest-stage variation; expression and GC-MS associations do not establish causal pathway steps.

title: Amorpha-4,11-diene synthase: a key enzyme in artemisinin biosynthesis and engineering.
evidence_scope: ADS function and artemisinin pathway engineering
decision_rationale: Published review is useful for pathway and engineering context; ADS presence alone cannot establish artemisinin production in another species.

title: Artemisinin as a therapeutic vs. its more complex Artemisia source material.
evidence_scope: comparison of purified artemisinin with complex Artemisia material
decision_rationale: Published review frames source-material, matrix, consistency, and translation questions; claims about whole-leaf therapy require primary clinical and pharmacokinetic verification.

title: Insecticidal Activity of a Component, (-)-4-Terpineol, Isolated from the Essential Oil of Artemisia lavandulaefolia DC. against Plutella xylostella (L.).
evidence_scope: defined A. lavandulaefolia constituent and insect assay
decision_rationale: Primary isolation and bioassay study provides stronger constituent attribution than whole-oil screening; insecticidal activity is not mammalian safety or antiparasitic efficacy.

title: AaMYB108 is the core factor integrating light and jasmonic acid signaling to regulate artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: light and jasmonate integration in artemisinin regulation
decision_rationale: Primary transcription-factor perturbation study informs environmental signaling in A. annua; network conservation and ecological generality remain untested.

title: Synergistic interaction of two bHLH transcription factors positively regulates artemisinin biosynthetic pathway in Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: cooperating bHLH transcription factors in artemisinin regulation
decision_rationale: Primary interaction and transgenic study informs combinatorial pathway control; engineered A. annua responses do not establish genus-wide regulatory architecture.

title: Metabolic engineering of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway in Artemisia annua and relation to the expression of the artemisinin biosynthetic pathway.
evidence_scope: cross-pathway engineering and artemisinin expression in A. annua
decision_rationale: Primary engineered-cell study informs pathway coupling and ROS-related artemisinin biology; anthocyanin manipulation is not evidence for native chemotype evolution.

title: Future antimalarials from Artemisia? A rationale for natural product mining against drug-refractory Plasmodium stages.
evidence_scope: Artemisia natural-product mining across Plasmodium stages
decision_rationale: Published review is useful for stage-aware antimalarial discovery and hypothesis generation; it does not substitute for primary stage-specific or clinical evidence.

title: JA-Regulated AaGSW1-AaYABBY5/AaWRKY9 Complex Regulates Artemisinin Biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: JA-responsive transcription-factor complex
decision_rationale: Primary protein-interaction and regulatory study informs trichome-localized artemisinin control; function outside A. annua remains unresolved.

title: Traditional uses, Phytochemistry, Pharmacology, and Toxicology of the Genus Artemisia L. (Asteraceae): A High-value Medicinal Plant.
evidence_scope: genus-level phytochemistry pharmacology and toxicology
decision_rationale: Published review is useful for discovery and safety context across Artemisia; broad pharmacological summaries require primary compound, preparation, and assay verification.

title: Genome-wide identification and expression profiling of MYB transcription factors in Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: A. argyi MYB family and terpenoid-related regulation
decision_rationale: Primary genome-wide candidate study extends transcriptional-regulatory coverage beyond A. annua; expression and motif inference do not establish target function or orthology.

title: Artemisia annua L. essential oil-loaded chitosan nanoparticles: synthesis, characterization, in-vitro release kinetics, and acetylcholinesterase inhibition as a mode of action against plant-parasitic nematodes.
evidence_scope: nanoformulated A. annua oil against plant-parasitic nematodes
decision_rationale: Primary formulation study informs delivery and nematode phenotype; nanoparticle-specific efficacy and safety cannot be generalized to free oil or purified terpenes.

title: Genome-Wide Analysis of Oxidosqualene Cyclase Genes in Artemisia annua: Evolution, Expression, and Potential Roles in Triterpenoid Biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: A. annua OSC gene family and triterpenoid biosynthesis
decision_rationale: Primary genome-wide OSC study expands C30 pathway evidence; predicted roles require enzyme and metabolite validation and do not establish antiparasitic activity.

title: Genome-wide analysis of the AarPDR gene family in Artemisia argyi and its potential role in regulating terpenoids transport.
evidence_scope: A. argyi PDR transporter family and terpenoid transport
decision_rationale: Primary comparative genomics study informs transport and compartment hypotheses; gene-family annotation and expression are not proof of substrate specificity.

title: Phytochemical characterization and insight into the in vitro anthelmintic activity of Artemisia brevifolia Wall ex Dc. against the different life stages of the gastrointestinal nematode of sheep.
evidence_scope: A. brevifolia chemistry and life-stage-resolved nematode assays
decision_rationale: Primary phytochemical and anthelmintic study directly expands species and parasite-stage coverage; constituent attribution and host translation require full-text extraction.

title: Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analysis reveals the coordinated regulatory mechanisms of artemisinin and flavonoid mediated by AaMYB8 in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: A. annua chemotype-integrated artemisinin/flavonoid regulation
decision_rationale: Primary integrated study informs matrix and co-regulation hypotheses; flavonoid association does not establish terpene synergy or clinical benefit.

title: Identification and quantification of sesquiterpenes, alkaloids, flavonoids and coumarins in Artemisia annua L: Potential artemisinin activity-enhancing compounds.
evidence_scope: untargeted A. annua sesquiterpene and co-metabolite profiling
decision_rationale: Primary quantitative profiling expands constituent coverage and activity-enhancement hypotheses; co-occurrence is not proof of synergy or antiparasitic causality.

title: Transcriptome and metabolome analyses revealed the main profiles contributing the mild aroma characteristics of Artemisia stolonifera.
evidence_scope: A. stolonifera aroma metabolomics and transcriptomics
decision_rationale: Primary integrated study adds an understudied species and links aroma profiles to candidate genes; product attribution and comparative orthology remain open.

title: Low phosphorus promotes caryophyllene biosynthesis by regulating AaTPS3 in Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: phosphorus-responsive AaTPS3 and caryophyllene biosynthesis
decision_rationale: Primary nutrient-perturbation study informs environmental regulation of an A. argyi sesquiterpene; fertilizer response is not evidence for parasite activity or universal ecology.

title: Differential effects of biologically and chemically synthesized copper oxide nanoparticles on artemisinin biosynthesis gene expression in Artemisia absinthium.
evidence_scope: nanoparticle stress and artemisinin-pathway expression in A. absinthium
decision_rationale: Primary stress-engineering study extends artemisinin regulation beyond A. annua; gene-expression induction does not establish safe production or pathway flux.

title: Sesquiterpene γ-lactones of plants of the Asteraceae family of the flora of Kazakhstan: Search, distribution, biological activity.
evidence_scope: Kazakhstan Asteraceae sesquiterpene-lactone distribution and activity
decision_rationale: Published regional synthesis supports STL discovery and distribution context; summarized biological activity requires primary verification and taxon-specific extraction.

title: Enhanced Synthesis of Polyphenols and Terpenes by UV-A Irradiation in Artemisia argyi Leaves.
evidence_scope: UV-A induction of A. argyi terpenes and polyphenols
decision_rationale: Primary environmental metabolomics/transcriptomics study informs stress-responsive chemotype shifts; induction is treatment-specific and not proof of antiparasitic activity.

title: Genome-Wide Characterization and Light-Responsive Expression Patterns of B-Box Transcription Factors in Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: A. argyi BBX family and light-responsive secondary metabolism
decision_rationale: Primary genome-wide regulatory study adds light-signaling candidates; expression patterns do not establish direct regulation of terpene enzymes.

title: Antimalarial Activity of Methoxylated Flavonoid Fraction (Cirsimaritin-Dominated) from Artemisia kopetdaghensis in Plasmodium berghei-Infected Mice with in silico Analysis.
evidence_scope: A. kopetdaghensis flavonoid fraction and murine malaria
decision_rationale: Primary antimalarial study is relevant matrix context but its dominant fraction is flavonoid rather than terpene; retain separate from terpene efficacy claims.

title: Nanoencapsulation of Artemisia annua Essential Oil in Chitosan-Lipid Carriers Enhances Stability, Larvicidal, Antifungal, and Anticancer Efficacy.
evidence_scope: nanoencapsulated A. annua oil delivery and larvicidal assays
decision_rationale: Primary formulation study informs stability and vector-control translation; carrier effects and mixture activity prevent attribution to individual terpenes.

title: HetCA/STOCSY-Guided Dereplication of Artemisia arborescens Reveals Furofuran Lignans with Antileishmanial Effects.
evidence_scope: A. arborescens dereplication and antileishmanial lignans
decision_rationale: Primary dereplication study expands species-level antiparasitic natural-product discovery; lignans are non-terpenes and must remain separately coded.

title: Artemisiyneolides A-K, Guaiane Sesquiterpenoid-Heptatriyne Hybrids through C-C Linkages from Artemisia sieversiana with Antihepatoma Activity.
evidence_scope: A. sieversiana guaiane sesquiterpenoid structural diversity
decision_rationale: Primary isolation and structure study expands unusual sesquiterpenoid chemistry; antihepatoma activity is not antiparasitic evidence.

title: AabHLH140 simultaneously enhances artemisinin and polymethoxylated flavonoid accumulation in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: co-regulation of artemisinin and flavonoids in A. annua
decision_rationale: Primary transcription-factor engineering study informs coordinated specialized metabolism; enhanced accumulation in A. annua does not establish synergy or cross-species conservation.

title: The chemotherapy of rodent malaria, XL. The action of artemisinin and related sesquiterpenes.
evidence_scope: early rodent-malaria pharmacology of artemisinin and related sesquiterpenes
decision_rationale: Primary historical pharmacology study anchors parasite-stage and derivative activity; it concerns defined compounds and cannot be generalized to crude Artemisia material.

title: Metabolite profiling of Artemisia afra and Artemisia annua extracts reveals divergent effects on Plasmodium falciparum.
evidence_scope: comparative malaria extract metabolomics and artemisinin-associated parasite responses
decision_rationale: Primary comparative metabolomics study informs species-specific extract effects; phenolic and matrix signals are not terpene-specific and do not establish a direct parasite target or clinical efficacy.

title: Dihydroartemisinic acid dehydrogenase-mediated alternative route for artemisinin biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: AaDHAADH enzyme characterization and engineered DHAA production
decision_rationale: Primary enzyme and metabolic-engineering study adds an alternative artemisinin-production route; engineered yeast output does not establish native in-planta flux or cross-species function.

title: Quantitative Estimation and Biosynthetic Pathways Study of Artemisinin in Artemisia tournefortiana: An Alternative Source for Artemisinin.
evidence_scope: A. tournefortiana tissue- and geography-specific artemisinin measurement and pathway-associated sequence comparison
decision_rationale: Primary cross-species chemistry/genetics study supports measured occurrence and candidate pathway potential; it does not establish therapeutic equivalence, native flux, or resistance behavior.

title: Catalytic Plasticity of Germacrene A Oxidase Underlies Sesquiterpene Lactone Diversification
evidence_scope: germacrene-A oxidase catalytic promiscuity and STL evolution
decision_rationale: Primary heterologous enzyme study provides an experimentally testable mechanism for STL diversification; native Artemisia pathway reconstruction and antiparasitic activity remain unresolved.

title: Effects of vegetative and flowering stages on the biosynthesis of artemisinin in Artemisia species
evidence_scope: cross-species phenology and artemisinin harvesting context
decision_rationale: Primary multi-species stage comparison informs tissue and harvest hypotheses; locality, genotype, and HPLC-only artemisinin measurements limit generalization to all terpenes or species.

title: Combination of artemisinin-based natural compounds from Artemisia annua L. for the treatment of malaria: Pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic studies
evidence_scope: defined artemisinin combination pharmacology in murine malaria
decision_rationale: Primary mouse PD/PK study supports a preparation-specific combination hypothesis; scopoletin is non-terpene, and the result is not clinical evidence or proof of single-component synergy.

title: Secondary Metabolites Isolated from Artemisia afra and Artemisia annua and Their Anti-Malarial, Anti-Inflammatory and Immunomodulating Properties-Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics: A Review
evidence_scope: malaria-focused review of Artemisia metabolites and PK/PD
decision_rationale: Review is useful for discovery and context across monoterpenes, sesquiterpenes, triterpenes, antimalarial activity, and toxicity; primary studies remain necessary for quantitative or causal claims.

title: Anthelmintic effects of Artemisia herba-alba and Artemisia judaica extracts on Ascaridia galli in poultry
evidence_scope: crude-extract poultry anthelmintic phenotype plus camphor docking hypotheses
decision_rationale: Primary in-vitro/in-vivo poultry study informs helminth efficacy and target prioritization; crude extract, species difference, and docking boundaries prevent terpene attribution or human vermifuge inference.

title: Analysis of sesquiterpene lactones, lignans, and flavonoids in wormwood (Artemisia absinthium L.) using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-mass spectrometry, reversed phase HPLC, and HPLC-solid phase extraction-nuclear magnetic resonance
evidence_scope: validated wormwood sesquiterpene-lactone analytical method and stability
decision_rationale: Primary analytical study supports preparation-aware measurement of wormwood lactones and degradation; occurrence and stability do not establish anthelmintic activity or safe dose.

title: Anthelmintic activity of Artemisia annua L. extracts in vitro and the effect of an aqueous extract and artemisinin in sheep naturally infected with gastrointestinal nematodes.
evidence_scope: preparation-specific A. annua extracts and artemisinin against H. contortus in vitro and in sheep
decision_rationale: Primary study provides an important negative/limited ovine translation control: in-vitro activity did not yield significant single-dose efficacy, and artemisinin malaria activity cannot be generalized to anthelmintic treatment.

title: Anthelmintic activity of Artemisia brevifolia in sheep
evidence_scope: dose-resolved A. brevifolia whole-plant anthelmintic assays and sheep trial
decision_rationale: Primary comparative veterinary study supports a dose trend and bounded EPG reduction, but crude chemistry, mixed infection, and lower activity than levamisole prevent terpene or human inference.

title: Trichomes + roots + ROS = artemisinin: regulating artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: artemisinin regulation by trichomes roots and reactive oxygen species
decision_rationale: Relevant review integrates tissue, precursor, redox, and regulatory context for artemisinin; it is a synthesis source and not a primary quantitative result.

title: Artemisinin biosynthesis and its regulatory enzymes: Progress and perspective
evidence_scope: artemisinin biosynthesis and regulatory enzymes
decision_rationale: Historical review is useful for pathway context and unresolved controversies; primary enzyme and perturbation studies remain the basis for mechanistic claims.

title: Microbial transformation of antimalarial terpenoids
evidence_scope: microbial transformation and medicinal chemistry of antimalarial terpenoids
decision_rationale: Review supports derivative and biotransformation context for artemisinin and related terpenoids; engineered or transformed products are not native Artemisia metabolites.

title: Considerations on the mechanism of action of artemisinin antimalarials: part 1--the 'carbon radical' and 'heme' hypotheses
evidence_scope: artemisinin activation and heme/carbon-radical mechanism hypotheses
decision_rationale: Mechanistic review supports explicit uncertainty around artemisinin action and resistance; it does not establish a sole parasite target.

title: Compositional Variability and Toxic Activity of Mugwort (Artemisia vulgaris) Essential Oils
evidence_scope: A. vulgaris population chemotypes and oil toxicity
decision_rationale: Primary fifteen-population study adds davanone and germacrene-D chemotypes plus brine-shrimp toxicity; oil composition and toxicity are population- and assay-specific.

title: Substrate promiscuity of enzymes from the sesquiterpene biosynthetic pathways from Artemisia annua and Tanacetum parthenium allows for novel combinatorial sesquiterpene production
evidence_scope: sesquiterpene-enzyme catalytic promiscuity and engineered sesquiterpene-lactone diversification
decision_rationale: Primary heterologous enzyme study supports catalytic opportunity and testable pathway-evolution hypotheses; engineered product formation is not proof of native flux or parasite activity.

title: Parallel Transcriptional Regulation of Artemisinin and Flavonoid Biosynthesis
evidence_scope: parallel regulation of artemisinin and flavonoid pathways
decision_rationale: Review supports co-regulation and matrix hypotheses; shared transcriptional control does not establish terpene-flavonoid synergy or clinical benefit.

title: In Vitro Anthelmintic Activity of Crude Extracts of Artemisia herba-alba and Punica granatum against Haemonchus contortus
evidence_scope: A. herba-alba crude-extract H. contortus assays
decision_rationale: Primary adult-motility and egg-hatch study expands comparative helminth evidence; crude extracts and absence of constituent attribution prevent transfer to wormwood or human use.

title: Transcriptome changes induced by abiotic stresses in Artemisia annua
evidence_scope: abiotic-stress effects on A. annua artemisinin and transcriptomes
decision_rationale: Primary stress experiment informs environment-dependent pathway regulation; altered artemisinin under tested conditions does not establish universal ecological response or safe production.

title: Carrageenan oligomers and salicylic acid act in tandem to escalate artemisinin production by suppressing arsenic uptake and oxidative stress in Artemisia annua (sweet wormwood) cultivated in high arsenic soil
evidence_scope: arsenic stress and elicitor effects on A. annua artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary stress-engineering study links oxidative physiology and artemisinin yield in two varieties; it is treatment- and environment-specific and not evidence of parasite efficacy.

title: Sesquiterpene Lactones from Artemisia absinthium. Biotransformation and Rearrangement of the Insect Antifeedant 3α-hydroxypelenolide
evidence_scope: wormwood sesquiterpene-lactone isolation biotransformation and insect antifeedant activity
decision_rationale: Primary structure and biotransformation study expands wormwood STL chemistry; insect antifeedant and cytotoxic endpoints do not establish anthelmintic efficacy.

title: Pharmacokinetic and tissue distribution study of eight volatile constituents in rats orally administrated with the essential oil of Artemisiae argyi Folium by GC-MS/MS
evidence_scope: A. argyi essential-oil volatile pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution
decision_rationale: Primary rat disposition study adds exposure context for eucalyptol thujone camphor borneol bornyl acetate eugenol beta-caryophyllene and caryophyllene oxide; it does not establish parasite efficacy or a safe human dose.

title: Pharmacokinetic study of artemisinin after oral intake of a traditional preparation of Artemisia annua L. (annual wormwood).
evidence_scope: human pharmacokinetics of artemisinin tea
decision_rationale: Fourteen-volunteer tea PK study provides a human matrix-exposure anchor; the authors explicitly did not establish tea as equivalent to modern artemisinin drugs.

title: Ancient Chinese methods are remarkably effective for the preparation of artemisinin-rich extracts of Qing Hao with potent antimalarial activity.
evidence_scope: preparation-dependent artemisinin extraction and malaria activity
decision_rationale: Primary preparation comparison separates concentration from total extraction and shows that only pounded juice suppressed P. berghei parasitemia; not a standardized clinical preparation.

title: Dried whole plant Artemisia annua as an antimalarial therapy.
evidence_scope: whole-plant versus pure artemisinin rodent malaria
decision_rationale: Primary rodent study reports greater efficacy and approximately 40-fold higher artemisinin bioavailability from dried leaves; this remains preclinical and matrix attribution is unresolved.

title: Is artemisinin the only antiplasmodial compound in the Artemisia annua tea infusion? An in vitro study.
evidence_scope: matched A. annua tea/nonpolar extract versus artemisinin in vitro
decision_rationale: Primary in-vitro comparison found activity closely followed artemisinin concentration and did not detect significant extract enhancement; this is one preparation and parasite-stage context.

title: Pharmacokinetics of artemisinin delivered by oral consumption of Artemisia annua dried leaves in healthy vs. Plasmodium chabaudi-infected mice.
evidence_scope: infected-versus-healthy mouse PK of dried-leaf artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary PK study shows infection and plant matrix change artemisinin exposure and metabolism; it is not a direct parasite-efficacy or human-safety study.

title: In vitro reduction of Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes: Artemisia spp. tea infusions vs. artemisinin.
evidence_scope: Artemisia tea effects on asexual parasites and gametocytes
decision_rationale: Primary stage-resolved in-vitro study found mainly artemisinin-dependent effects with a weak artemisinin-deficient A. afra signal; no clinical or single-terpene inference.

title: In vitro analyses of Artemisia extracts on Plasmodium falciparum suggest a complex antimalarial effect.
evidence_scope: extract activity across malaria strains and host-serum context
decision_rationale: Primary strain- and exposure-time comparison reports a possible host interaction; serum effects and crude extracts prevent direct assignment to a terpene or defined target.

title: Artemisinin-independent inhibitory activity of Artemisia sp. infusions against different Plasmodium stages including relapse-causing hypnozoites.
evidence_scope: Artemisia infusion effects across blood liver and hypnozoite stages
decision_rationale: Primary comparative stage study reports artemisinin-independent infusion activity, including hypnozoite disruption; exact active chemistry and clinical translation remain unresolved.

title: Artemisia extracts differ from artemisinin effects on human hepatic CYP450s 2B6 and 3A4 in vitro.
evidence_scope: Artemisia tea effects on human CYP2B6 and CYP3A4
decision_rationale: Primary human hepatic-cell and microsome study separates artemisinin transcriptional induction from extract-mediated activity inhibition; this informs interaction risk, not antiparasitic efficacy.

title: Dried Leaf Artemisia Annua Improves Bioavailability of Artemisinin via Cytochrome P450 Inhibition and Enhances Artemisinin Efficacy Downstream.
evidence_scope: plant-matrix CYP inhibition and artemisinin exposure
decision_rationale: Primary HLM and rat study supports a bioavailability mechanism and sex-dependent downstream effects; it does not identify the responsible phytochemical or establish a regimen.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of Artemisia absinthium against Hymenolepis nana: in vitro and in vivo studies in comparison with the anthelmintic praziquantel.
evidence_scope: wormwood aqueous extract against tapeworm in vitro and mice
decision_rationale: Primary wormwood study reports dose-dependent adult-worm damage and reduced EPG/worm burden, with praziquantel best; crude extract prevents terpene attribution and human inference.

title: Antiparasitic efficiency of Artemisia absinthium on Toxocara cati in naturally infected cats.
evidence_scope: wormwood extract in naturally infected cats
decision_rationale: Primary veterinary study reports declining fecal egg counts during seven-day dosing and no reported chemistry abnormality, but no inhibition of embryonation in vitro; efficacy and safety require replication.

title: In vitro evidence that the pastoral Artemisia campestris species exerts an anthelmintic effect on Haemonchus contortus from sheep.
evidence_scope: A. campestris extract effects on H. contortus eggs and adults
decision_rationale: Primary extract study found strong egg-hatch and adult mortality effects while chemistry was flavonoid-dominated; it is comparative helminth evidence, not terpene causality.

title: Anthelmintic properties of extracts from Artemisia plants against nematodes.
evidence_scope: A. indica and A. roxburghiana methanol extracts against mixed gastrointestinal nematodes
decision_rationale: Primary in-vitro screen reports modest concentration-dependent activity and calls for purification and in-vivo confirmation; the abstract does not support terpene attribution.

title: In Vitro Nematocidal Effect and Anthelmintic Activity of Artemisia cina Against Haemonchus contortus in Gerbils and Relative Expression of Hc29 Gene in Transitional Larvae (L3-L4).
evidence_scope: A. cina extracts and isoguaiacine against H. contortus
decision_rationale: Primary staged assay and gerbil study identifies n-hexane extract/isoguaiacine activity and Hc29 expression changes; target expression and docking-style hypotheses do not establish direct binding.

title: Allele-aware chromosome-level genome assembly of Artemisia annua reveals the correlation between ADS expansion and artemisinin yield.
evidence_scope: allele-aware A. annua genome and ADS copy-number/artemisinin relationship
decision_rationale: Primary chromosome-level comparative-genomics study links ADS copy number with artemisinin content across contrasting haplotypes and 36 samples; correlation is not proof of causal flux or cross-species equivalence.

title: Comment on the paper \Chemical analyses and anthelmintic effects of Artemisia campestris essential oil\"."
evidence_scope: methodological commentary on A. campestris essential-oil anthelmintic evidence
decision_rationale: Commentary is retained to audit interpretation of a focal helminth study; no abstract was available and no new quantitative result is extracted.

title: The anthelmintic efficacy of Artemisia herba-alba against Haemonchus contortus infection in goats.
evidence_scope: A. herba-alba powdered shoots in experimentally infected goats
decision_rationale: Primary older goat study reports marked clinical, fecal, and necropsy responses in most treated goats but incomplete suppression in two animals; chemistry and dose standardization are unresolved.

title: Screening of Artemisia absinthium for antimalarial effects on Plasmodium berghei in mice: a preliminary report.
evidence_scope: metadata-only historical wormwood malaria record
decision_rationale: No abstract was available; retained as a historical lead for full-text retrieval, not as quantitative evidence.

title: Artemisinin in traditional tea preparations of Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: metadata-only tea chemistry record
decision_rationale: No abstract was available; retained as a historical lead for full-text retrieval, not as quantitative evidence.

title: Thirteen-week repeated dose toxicity study of wormwood (Artemisia absinthium) extract in rats.
evidence_scope: repeated-dose wormwood toxicology
decision_rationale: Primary rat toxicology study reports no obvious treatment-related toxicity at tested concentrations and a study-specific NOAEL estimate; this does not define human safety or thujone risk for all preparations.

title: In vivo antimalarial efficacy of Artemisia afra powder suspensions.
evidence_scope: A. afra powder in rodent malaria and translation controversy
decision_rationale: Primary mouse study did not support the proposed artemisinin-independent prodrug hypothesis for A. afra, providing an important counterweight to in-vitro infusion findings; not human efficacy.

title: Evaluation of the ovicidal activity and fasciolicidal activity of the extract of ethyl acetate from Artemisia ludoviciana Nutt. spp. mexicana and of artemisinin against adult parasites of Fasciola hepatica.
evidence_scope: A. ludoviciana extract and artemisinin against Fasciola hepatica
decision_rationale: Primary fluke and egg assay adds a comparative Artemisia helminth phenotype; extract chemistry and direct artemisinin contribution require resolution.

title: Understanding Artemisia cina Ethyl Acetate Extract's Anthelmintic Effect on Haemonchus contortus Eggs and L3 Larvae: The Synergism of Peruvin Binary Mixtures.
evidence_scope: defined A. cina compound-mixture synergy against H. contortus
decision_rationale: Primary isolation and binary-mixture study provides a stronger constituent-to-phenotype bridge; synergy is concentration- and pair-specific and requires host-selectivity testing.

title: The anthelmintic activity of the white wormwood (Artemisia herba Alba) against Haemonchus contortus in beef cattle.
evidence_scope: A. herba-alba aqueous extract adult-worm assay
decision_rationale: Primary in-vitro cattle-worm assay reports concentration-dependent motility loss and mortality, including complete killing at one tested concentration; no in-vivo efficacy or terpene attribution.

title: In vitro and in vivo anthelmintic activity of Artemisia absinthium against gastrointestinal nematodes of free-grazing goats from Ayacucho, Peru.
evidence_scope: wormwood extract against goat gastrointestinal nematodes
decision_rationale: Primary recent goat study reports strong in-vitro larval effects but no significant fecal-egg-count reduction at the tested in-vivo dose; a key translation boundary.

title: Artemisia vulgaris anthelmintic activities to ova and adult stages of Fasciola gigantica in vitro.
evidence_scope: A. vulgaris extract against Fasciola gigantica eggs and adults
decision_rationale: Primary in-vitro fluke study reports concentration- and time-dependent ovicidal and flukicidal effects with morphology changes; active compounds and mechanism remain unresolved.

title: Isolation of potent antileishmanial agents from Artemisia kermanensis Podlech using bioguided fractionation.
evidence_scope: bioguided A. kermanensis fractionation against Leishmania major
decision_rationale: Primary structure-confirmed fractionation identifies flavonoid antileishmanial leads with low macrophage toxicity; the principal active compounds are not terpenes and require independent confirmation.

title: Enhanced Antimalarial Activity of Extracts of Artemisia annua L. Achieved with Aqueous Solutions of Salicylate Salts and Ionic Liquids.
evidence_scope: hydrotrope-assisted A. annua extraction and in-vitro malaria activity
decision_rationale: Primary extraction-method study reports artemisinin-rich extracts with higher P. falciparum activity than pure artemisinin in its tested system; solvent effects, matrix composition, and clinical translation remain unresolved.

title: Artemisia annua L. and photoresponse: from artemisinin accumulation, volatile profile and anatomical modifications to gene expression.
evidence_scope: light quality effects on trichomes volatile diversity and artemisinin pathway expression
decision_rationale: Primary controlled light-response study links blue/yellow light to anatomy, volatile diversity, ADS expression, and artemisinin accumulation; treatment-specific association is not a universal production rule.

title: Characterization of high-artemisinin yielding Artemisia annua bioecotypes using gene-specific STS markers and HPLC for quality-oriented selection.
evidence_scope: marker-assisted high-artemisinin bioecotype selection
decision_rationale: Primary marker/HPLC study supports within-species selection and links STS markers to artemisinin yield; causal alleles and cross-environment stability remain unproven.

title: AaSPATULA synergistically coordinates glandular trichome initiation and vegetative growth to maximize whole-plant artemisinin yield in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: trichome initiation and artemisinin-yield regulation
decision_rationale: Primary perturbation study links AaSPATULA to glandular trichome density, growth, and artemisinin accumulation; it does not establish parasite activity or universal transfer across genotypes.

title: Exploring Chemical Variability in the Essential Oil of Artemisia absinthium L. in Relation to Different Phenological Stages and Geographical Location.
evidence_scope: wormwood essential-oil geography and phenology
decision_rationale: Primary chemotype study resolves site- and stage-dependent volatile shifts; it does not identify stable species-wide markers or anthelmintic actives.

title: Low-Thujone A. absinthium L. (Wormwood) Essential Oils and Extracts with Potential Antioxidative/Prooxidant Activity.
evidence_scope: low-thujone wormwood chemistry and safety
decision_rationale: Primary analytical study documents a low-thujone oil dominated by trans-sabinyl acetate; one low-thujone lot cannot represent all wormwood products or establish human safety.

title: Chemical variability for authenticated and commercial Artemisia absinthium L. essential oils with thujones on tephritid fruit flies: Mediterranean fruit fly Ceratitis capitata (Wiedemann) and Caribbean fruit fly Anastrepha suspensa (Loew).
evidence_scope: authenticated versus commercial wormwood oils and thujone bioactivity
decision_rationale: Primary comparison shows commercial/authenticated chemotype variability and insect endpoints; insect toxicity is not a human safety or helminth-efficacy surrogate.

title: Validating a sensitive LCMS method for the quantitation of artemisinin in Artemisia spp. including material used in retracted clinical trials.
evidence_scope: artemisinin analytical validation and contamination control
decision_rationale: Validated LC-MS provides a quality-control anchor and detects likely cross-contamination; analyte detection alone does not establish identity, efficacy, or safety.

title: Standardized Artemisia annua Exhibits Dual Antileishmanial Activity and Immunomodulatory Potential In Vitro.
evidence_scope: standardized A. annua extract against Leishmania infantum
decision_rationale: Primary standardized-extract assay includes promastigote, amastigote, macrophage, and cytokine endpoints; activity remains mixture-level and requires in-vivo and constituent-resolved confirmation.

title: Antiparasitic Activity of Silver Nanoparticles Synthesized from Artemisia cina Aqueous Extract Against Haemonchus contortus.
evidence_scope: formulated A. cina nanoparticle activity against H. contortus
decision_rationale: Primary AgNP study reports larval mortality and oxidative-enzyme effects, but the formulated nanoparticle is not equivalent to native extract or terpene activity.

title: The Beneficial Use of Artemisia annua, Artemisinin, and Other Compounds in Animal Health.
evidence_scope: Artemisia and artemisinin in animal health
decision_rationale: Review context supports standardization and species-appropriate evidence requirements; it does not substitute for primary veterinary efficacy or terpene-specific studies.

title: Effects of LEDs, macronutrients and culture conditions on biomass and artemisinin production using Artemisia annua L. suspension cultures.
evidence_scope: culture conditions and artemisinin production
decision_rationale: Primary controlled-culture study supports process-development hypotheses linking light/nutrients to biomass and artemisinin; effects do not automatically predict field chemotypes.

title: Phytochemical Analysis, Antioxidant Potential, and Cytotoxicity Evaluation of Traditionally Used Artemisia absinthium L. (Wormwood) Growing in the Central Region of Saudi Arabia.
evidence_scope: regional wormwood volatile chemistry and cytotoxicity
decision_rationale: Primary Saudi oil study supplies a defined cis-davanone-rich chemotype and cell-assay safety context; it cannot establish species-wide safety or anthelmintic mechanism.

title: TrichomeLess Regulator 3 is required for trichome initial and cuticle biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: trichome and cuticle regulation
decision_rationale: Primary genetic/regulatory study connects TLR3 to trichome initiation, cuticle biosynthesis, and artemisinin-associated phenotypes; parasite relevance remains untested.

title: AaMYC3 bridges the regulation of glandular trichome density and artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: AaMYC3 regulation of trichome density and artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary transcription-factor perturbation links jasmonate-responsive AaMYC3 to trichome density and pathway genes; this is plant-side evidence, not direct parasite target evidence.

title: Novel Differentially Expressed LncRNAs Regulate Artemisinin Biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: lncRNA associations with artemisinin biosynthesis
decision_rationale: Primary transcriptomic study identifies differentially expressed lncRNAs associated with ADS/DXS/HMGS and high/low artemisinin material; direct regulation and evolutionary conservation remain unresolved.

title: Recovery and Economic Aspects of Extraction Methods for Artemisinin and its Precursors from Artemisia annua L. Leaves.
evidence_scope: artemisinin extraction recovery and standardization
decision_rationale: Review context compares solvent/process tradeoffs and supports product-level fingerprinting; extraction recovery is not equivalent to bioavailability, efficacy, or safety.

title: Exogenous abscisic acid mediates ROS homeostasis and maintains glandular trichome to enhance artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua under copper toxicity.
evidence_scope: ABA rescue of copper-stress effects on trichomes and artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary stress/hormone study links ABA rescue to trichome and artemisinin changes under copper toxicity; treatment-specific effects do not establish a stable chemotype or parasite phenotype.

title: TRICHOME AND ARTEMISININ REGULATOR 1 Is Required for Trichome Development and Artemisinin Biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: TAR1 trichome and artemisinin regulation
decision_rationale: Primary perturbation and promoter-assay study links TAR1 to trichome morphology, cuticular wax, ADS/CYP71AV1, and artemisinin; cross-species function remains open.

title: Effects of overexpression of AaWRKY1 on artemisinin biosynthesis in transgenic Artemisia annua plants.
evidence_scope: AaWRKY1 regulation of CYP71AV1 and artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary transgenic study provides a trichome-specific regulation anchor; construct and genetic background limit native or evolutionary inference.

title: Cloning and characterization of AabHLH1, a bHLH transcription factor that positively regulates artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: AabHLH1 E-box promoter binding
decision_rationale: Primary promoter-binding and transactivation study supports plant-side regulation but not native flux or conserved cross-species function.

title: Overexpression of artemisinic aldehyde Δ11 (13) reductase gene-enhanced artemisinin and its relative metabolite biosynthesis in transgenic Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: DBR2 pathway engineering
decision_rationale: Primary transgenic chemistry study shows increased target and competing-branch metabolites; it is not a one-enzyme yield rule.

title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza increase artemisinin accumulation in Artemisia annua by higher expression of key biosynthesis genes via enhanced jasmonic acid levels.
evidence_scope: mycorrhiza and jasmonate regulation
decision_rationale: Primary plant-microbe study links colonization, JA, trichomes, and artemisinin; environmental context and causal transfer require replication.

title: AaEIN3 Mediates the Downregulation of Artemisinin Biosynthesis by Ethylene Signaling Through Promoting Leaf Senescence in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: ethylene and senescence regulation
decision_rationale: Primary perturbation study identifies AaEIN3 as a negative plant-side regulator; it does not establish evolutionary divergence or parasite potency.

title: The SPB-Box Transcription Factor AaSPL2 Positively Regulates Artemisinin Biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: AaSPL2 and DBR2 promoter regulation
decision_rationale: Primary promoter and transgenic evidence supports AaSPL2 regulation; effect size is construct- and background-dependent.

title: The Transcription Factor Aabzip9 Positively Regulates the Biosynthesis of Artemisinin in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: AabZIP9 promoter binding and pathway regulation
decision_rationale: Primary transcription-factor study supports ADS-associated regulation; it does not establish conserved function or antiparasitic activity.

title: Artemisinin Biosynthesis in Non-glandular Trichome Cells of Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: non-glandular tissue localization of artemisinin biosynthesis
decision_rationale: Primary LC-MS and imaging study revises the glandular-trichome-only model in inbred and glandless material; broader species transfer remains untested.

title: Transcriptome analyses revealed the ultraviolet B irradiation and phytohormone gibberellins coordinately promoted the accumulation of artemisinin in Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: UV-B and gibberellin response
decision_rationale: Primary transcriptome/metabolome study links combined treatment to artemisinin and candidate TF modules; co-expression is not direct regulation.

title: [Relative expression of genes involved in artemisinin biosynthesis and artemisinin accumulation in different tissues of Artemisia annua].
evidence_scope: tissue-specific artemisinin expression and content
decision_rationale: Primary tissue comparison supports leaf/flower contrasts and ADS association; bulk tissue is not secretory-cell flux.

title: Earlier flowering induced by over-expression of CO gene does not accompany increase of artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: flowering-time perturbation and artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary developmental perturbation separates flowering time from artemisinin accumulation; it is a useful negative regulatory control.

title: Seasonal and Differential Sesquiterpene Accumulation in Artemisia annua Suggest Selection Based on Both Artemisinin and Dihydroartemisininic Acid may Increase Artemisinin in planta.
evidence_scope: seasonal chemotypes and ART/DHAA selection
decision_rationale: Primary multi-germplasm field study supports preflowering and complementary chemotype selection hypotheses; it does not provide pooled species means.

title: Assessment of Iranian endemic Artemisia khorassanica: karyological, genome size, and gene expressions involved in artemisinin production.
evidence_scope: polyploidy and negative artemisinin comparator
decision_rationale: Primary population study found diploid and tetraploid A. khorassanica without detectable artemisinin and with DBR2 silencing in autotetraploids; pathway absence is not fully proven.

title: Ovicidal and larvicidal activity of extracts from medicinal-plants against Haemonchus contortus
evidence_scope: comparative wormwood extract activity against H. contortus eggs and larvae
decision_rationale: Primary multi-plant assay identifies methanolic A. absinthium as one of the strongest preparations and measures selected secondary metabolites; the abstract does not establish terpene causality or in-vivo efficacy.

title: The Effects of Allium sativum L., Artemisia absinthium L., Cucurbita pepo L., Coriandrum sativum L., Satureja hortensis L. and Calendula officinalis L. on the Embryogenesis of Ascaris suum Eggs during an In Vitro Experimental Study
evidence_scope: wormwood extract activity against Ascaris suum embryogenesis and larval development
decision_rationale: Primary concentration-series comparison reports strong A. absinthium activity and mixed metabolite classes including sesquiterpene lactones; active constituent and parasite target remain unresolved.

title: Secondary Metabolites and Their Cytotoxic Activity of Artemisia nitrosa Weber. and Artemisia marschalliana Spreng
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed sesquiterpene-lactone isolation from A. nitrosa
decision_rationale: Primary MS/NMR study characterized a new germacrane-type lactone and known sesquiterpenes; the reported macrophage/cytotoxic assays are non-parasitic and do not establish an antiparasitic lead.

title: Sesquiterpene Lactones and Flavonoid from the Leaves of Basin Big Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata subsp. tridentata): Isolation, Characterization and Biological Activities
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed STL isolation from A. tridentata
decision_rationale: Primary leaf-fractionation study expands confirmed Artemisia STL chemistry; subspecies, tissue, and non-parasitic assay boundaries prevent transfer to wormwood or parasite efficacy.

title: Sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia vulgaris L. as potential NO inhibitors in LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophage cells
evidence_scope: germacranolide and guaianolide isolation from A. vulgaris
decision_rationale: Primary NMR/ECD/X-ray study isolated twelve new and ten known guaianolides with macrophage NO-inhibition data; this is structure and host-cell evidence, not antiparasitic activity.

title: Sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia verlotorum and their anti-inflammatory activities.
evidence_scope: structural diversity of A. verlotorum sesquiterpene lactones
decision_rationale: Primary whole-plant isolation study characterized new and known lactones with stereochemical evidence and macrophage activity; structural novelty does not establish parasite activity or cross-species pathway conservation.

title: Genome sequencing reveals chromosome fusion and extensive expansion of genes related to secondary metabolism in Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: A. argyi genome, ploidy, TPS expansion, and secondary metabolism
decision_rationale: Primary chromosome-level genome study reports an 8.03-Gb allotetraploid assembly, 135 TPS genes, and tandem expansion; assembly and annotation differences require caution in cross-study copy-number comparisons.

title: Quantification of santonin in eight species of Artemisia from Kazakhstan by means of HPLC-UV: Method development and validation.
evidence_scope: cross-species santonin quantitation and analytical validation
decision_rationale: Primary validated HPLC study supports lot- and species-specific santonin measurement, including A. absinthium; it is not an efficacy study or pooled abundance estimate.

title: ent-kauranoid diterpenes from Artemisia sacrorum.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed A. sacrorum diterpenes
decision_rationale: Primary isolation study expands C20 diterpene coverage; no antiparasitic endpoint or cross-species pathway conclusion is supported.

title: A new triterpenoid saponin from Artemisia sphaerocephala.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed A. sphaerocephala triterpenoid saponin
decision_rationale: Primary whole-plant isolation study expands C30 chemical space; no parasite or biosynthetic-function endpoint is reported.

title: Triterpenoids with α-glucosidase inhibitory activity from Artemisia argyi.
evidence_scope: A. argyi triterpene isolation and alpha-glucosidase assay
decision_rationale: Primary isolation study confirms nordammarane and cycloartane triterpenoids; alpha-glucosidase inhibition is not antiparasitic evidence.

title: Sesquiterpenoids and triterpenoids with anti-inflammatory effects from Artemisia vulgaris L.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed A. vulgaris sesquiterpene/triterpene diversity
decision_rationale: Primary spectroscopy and host-cell assay study broadens nonvolatile class coverage; inflammatory activity does not establish parasite activity or pathway homology.

title: A haploid pseudo-chromosome genome assembly for a keystone sagebrush species of western North American rangelands.
evidence_scope: A. tridentata genome assembly and polyploidy context
decision_rationale: Primary genome resource adds a third Artemisia evolutionary anchor; no terpene-family or parasite inference is made without common annotation and phenotype data.

title: Utilizing a comparative approach to assess genome evolution during diploidization in Artemisia tridentata, a keystone species of western North America.
evidence_scope: comparative A. tridentata/A. annua genome evolution
decision_rationale: Primary comparative study informs rearrangement, synteny, and diploidization context; it does not establish terpene-locus orthology or antiparasitic function.

title: One-step, two-step: Whole-genome-duplication pathways in Artemisia tridentata and potential consequences for genome evolution.
evidence_scope: A. tridentata WGD pathways and cytotype evolution
decision_rationale: Primary 2026 study supports ploidy-aware sampling and triploid-bridge hypotheses; it is not a terpene-pathway or parasite study.

title: Antiparasitic efficacy of Artemisia absinthium, toltrazuril and amprolium against intestinal coccidiosis in goats.
evidence_scope: A. absinthium crude-extract coccidiosis comparison in naturally infected goats
decision_rationale: Primary veterinary protozoan study provides a negative/limited translation control: the extract was less efficacious than standard drugs and did not resolve active chemistry.

title: A new chemical tool for absinthe producers, quantification of α/β-thujone and the bitter components in Artemisia absinthium.
evidence_scope: phenology-linked quantitative thujone and bitter-compound chemistry
decision_rationale: Primary analytical study directly supports harvest-stage and lot-specific wormwood chemistry; it does not establish parasite efficacy or safety.

title: Toxic essential oils. Part V: Behaviour modulating and toxic properties of thujones and thujone-containing essential oils of Salvia officinalis L., Artemisia absinthium L., Thuja occidentalis L. and Tanacetum vulgare L.
evidence_scope: thujone-containing oil composition paired with animal and toxicity endpoints
decision_rationale: Primary mixture-toxicology study shows that non-thujone constituents contribute to observed endpoints; it strengthens the preparation-specific safety boundary.

title: Intraspecific Variability of Wormwood (Artemisia absinthium L.) Occurring in Poland in Respect of Developmental and Chemical Traits.
evidence_scope: 11-population ex-situ wormwood chemotype and developmental comparison
decision_rationale: Primary population-level chemistry study quantifies oil and nonvolatile variation and directly informs wormwood chemotype stratification; beginning-of-flowering and ex-situ conditions limit generalization.

title: Selective nematocidal effects of essential oils from two cultivated Artemisia absinthium populations.
evidence_scope: thujone-free wormwood oils against Trichinella spiralis and Meloidogyne javanica
decision_rationale: Primary population-specific oil assay includes ex vivo infectivity, in vivo adult-worm reduction, and mammalian-cell counterassay; selective activity does not identify the active terpene or transfer to thujone-rich chemotypes.

title: Antimalarial activity of Artemisia nilagirica against Plasmodium falciparum.
evidence_scope: solvent-resolved A. nilagirica leaf extracts against P. falciparum
decision_rationale: Primary antiplasmodial extract study reports solvent-dependent IC50 values; phytochemical attribution, host selectivity, and clinical translation remain unresolved.

title: Chemical composition and larvicidal activity of essential oil of Artemisia gilvescens against Anopheles anthropophagus.
evidence_scope: Artemisia oil and defined major constituents against an Anopheles vector
decision_rationale: Primary chemistry-plus-larvicidal study supports a vector-control phenotype and constituent prioritization; it is not parasite-stage or human-safety evidence.

title: Purification and characterization of an enzyme involved in biochemical transformation of arteannuin B to artemisinin from Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: arteannuin B to artemisinin biochemical conversion
decision_rationale: Primary purified-enzyme assay supplies a step-level pathway anchor; historical protein characterization does not establish gene identity, native flux, or cross-species function.

title: Influence of plant growth stage on the essential oil content and composition in Davana (Artemisia pallens wall.).
evidence_scope: developmental and seasonal variation in A. pallens essential oil
decision_rationale: Primary two-season phenology study demonstrates harvest-stage effects on davanone and other volatiles; it does not establish antiparasitic activity.

title: Genome size in 21 Artemisia L. species (Asteraceae, Anthemideae): systematic, evolutionary, and ecological implications.
evidence_scope: genus-wide genome-size and ploidy context
decision_rationale: Primary comparative cytometry study supports ploidy-aware sampling and evolutionary covariates; genome size is not a terpene-gene count or chemistry measurement.

title: The genetics of artemisinin content in Artemisia annua L. and the breeding of high yielding cultivars.
evidence_scope: within-species quantitative genetics of artemisinin content
decision_rationale: Primary breeding study supports heritable variation and selection context; reported associations do not identify causal loci or guarantee yield across environments.

title: Crystal structure of artemisinic acid: a possible biogenetic precursor of antimalarial artemisinin from Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: artemisinic acid isolation and structure
decision_rationale: Primary isolation and X-ray structure paper supplies a historical sesquiterpene precursor anchor; it does not prove complete in-planta biosynthetic flux or antiparasitic activity.

title: Production of Artemisinin and Related Sesquiterpenes in Japanese Artemisia annua During a Vegetation Period.
evidence_scope: seasonal and positional artemisinin-related chemistry
decision_rationale: Primary wild-derived accession study measures seasonal and positional variation in artemisinin and related sesquiterpenes; it is not a universal harvest or climate experiment.

title: Salicylic acid activates artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: salicylic-acid elicitation and pathway regulation
decision_rationale: Primary perturbation study links SA, ROS, pathway-gene responses, and artemisinin accumulation; field relevance and parasite-potency transfer remain unresolved.

title: Trichome-specific expression of the amorpha-4,11-diene 12-hydroxylase (cyp71av1) gene, encoding a key enzyme of artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua, as reported by a promoter-GUS fusion.
evidence_scope: CYP71AV1 promoter and trichome localization
decision_rationale: Primary promoter-reporter study supports tissue- and age-specific regulation and variety differences; reporter activity is not native flux or cross-species function.

title: RNAi down-regulation of cinnamate-4-hydroxylase increases artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: phenylpropanoid and salicylic-acid pathway cross-talk
decision_rationale: Primary RNAi and feeding study supports pathway cross-talk and artemisinin modulation; pleiotropic stress effects and antiparasitic consequences were not tested.

title: Detailed Phytochemical Analysis of High- and Low Artemisinin-Producing Chemotypes of Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: high- versus low-artemisinin chemotype metabolomics
decision_rationale: Primary NMR/metabolomics study resolves more than 80 compounds and DBR2-associated saturated versus unsaturated sesquiterpene profiles; chemotype contrast is not a parasite assay.

title: Deciphering transcriptome profiles of tetraploid Artemisia annua plants with high artemisinin content.
evidence_scope: autotetraploid morphology transcriptome and artemisinin
decision_rationale: Primary induced-polyploid comparison supports ploidy-associated transcript and metabolite shifts; genetic background, biomass tradeoffs, and causal genes require validation.

title: Eco-friendly control of the poultry red mite, Dermanyssus gallinae (Dermanyssidae), using the α-thujone-rich essential oil of Artemisia sieberi (Asteraceae): toxic and repellent potential.
evidence_scope: thujone-rich Artemisia oil against an ectoparasite
decision_rationale: Primary GC/GC-MS plus contact, fumigant, repellent, and residual assays support an ectoparasite-control phenotype; they do not establish wormwood vermifuge efficacy, poultry safety, or single-constituent causality.

title: Sesquiterpene lactones from shoot culture of Artemisia aucheri with cytotoxicity against prostate and breast cancer cells.
evidence_scope: isolated eudesmanolide from Artemisia shoot culture
decision_rationale: Primary isolation paper expands STL chemical coverage with artemin; cancer-cell cytotoxicity is not antiparasitic efficacy or a therapeutic-window estimate.

title: Determination of artemisinin in Artemisia sieberi and anticoccidial effects of the plant extract in broiler chickens.
evidence_scope: A. sieberi artemisinin occurrence and species-specific Eimeria assay
decision_rationale: Primary HPLC-linked veterinary study adds a season- and parasite-specific artemisinin/anticoccidial record; extract composition and host-safety boundaries prevent human or single-constituent inference.

title: Acaricidal properties of Artemisia absinthium and Tanacetum vulgare (Asteraceae) essential oils obtained by three methods of extraction.
evidence_scope: extraction-method-dependent A. absinthium oil composition and acaricide potency
decision_rationale: Primary three-method oil comparison directly supports preparation-aware wormwood chemistry; the candidate C15H24 sesquiterpene remains association-level and is not helminth or human evidence.

title: Antimalarial principles from Artemisia indica.
evidence_scope: activity-guided A. indica non-terpene antimalarial isolation
decision_rationale: Primary purified exiguaflavone study supplies a useful non-terpene malaria control and prevents forced attribution of Artemisia antimalarial activity to terpenes.

title: [Studies on the antimalarial action of gelatin capsule of Artemisia annua].
evidence_scope: historical crude-preparation malaria report
decision_rationale: PubMed-indexed historical preparation study is retained for context with limited modern metadata, no constituent attribution, and no current clinical inference.

title: The cold-induced transcription factor bHLH112 promotes artemisinin biosynthesis indirectly via ERF1 in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: cold-induced bHLH112/ERF1 regulation of artemisinin biosynthesis
decision_rationale: Primary transcription-factor perturbation study adds an environment-responsive regulatory node; indirect regulation and A. annua-specific function remain explicit.

title: Chromatin Accessibility Is Associated with Artemisinin Biosynthesis Regulation in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: glandular-trichome versus leaf chromatin accessibility at artemisinin-pathway loci
decision_rationale: Primary ATAC-seq study supports an epigenomic and tissue-compartment hypothesis; accessibility is associative and does not establish flux or parasite activity.

title: Terpenes from Artemisia herba-alba.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed monoterpene-dimer and sesquiterpene-lactone isolation from A. herba-alba
decision_rationale: Primary NMR/HRMS isolation study fills class-balanced chemical coverage; no parasite endpoint or cross-species pathway inference is assigned.

title: Green Extraction of Volatile Terpenes from Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: supercritical-CO2, hydrodistillation, and steam-distillation comparison of A. annua volatile chemistry
decision_rationale: Primary controlled extraction study demonstrates process-dependent mono- and sesquiterpene profiles and is directly relevant to preparation-aware interpretation; no antiparasitic causality is assigned.

title: Comparative Analysis of Plastomes of Artemisia and Insights into the Infra-Generic Phylogenetic Relationships Within the Genus.
evidence_scope: infra-generic Artemisia plastome phylogeny
decision_rationale: Primary plastome comparison provides phylogenetic context for sampling but cannot substitute for nuclear gene trees or terpene-pathway orthology.

title: Anthelmintic activity of extracts of Artemisia absinthium against ovine nematodes.
evidence_scope: A. absinthium crude aqueous and ethanolic extracts against ovine gastrointestinal nematodes
decision_rationale: Primary in-vitro adult-worm motility and in-vivo sheep fecal-egg-count study directly supports the wormwood vermifuge evidence stream; extraction chemistry, active constituent, and human translation remain unresolved.

title: Anthelmintic Activity of Wormwood (Artemisia absinthium L.) and Mallow (Malva sylvestris L.) against Haemonchus contortus in Sheep.
evidence_scope: dry wormwood dietary supplementation, aqueous egg-hatch assay, and lamb H. contortus trial
decision_rationale: Primary study provides a positive in-vitro ovicidal signal but a nonsignificant group-level in-vivo lamb outcome; it is a key translation boundary and does not establish a terpene mechanism.

title: Comparison of in vivo anthelmintic efficacy of Artemisia absinthium extract and albendazole in Awassi breed sheep with natural gastrointestinal nematode infection.
evidence_scope: recent crude ethanolic A. absinthium extract versus albendazole in naturally infected Awassi sheep
decision_rationale: Primary contemporary veterinary FECRT and clinical-safety study; regional chemistry, small sample size, residue exposure, and lack of terpene attribution limit generalization.

title: The Genome of Artemisia annua Provides Insight into the Evolution of Asteraceae Family and Artemisinin Biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: A. annua draft genome, terpene-biosynthesis gene expansion, and artemisinin regulatory network
decision_rationale: Primary genome and transcriptome study directly anchors the evolutionary and pathway sections; the large gene count and predicted expansion require assembly- and annotation-aware comparison rather than direct copy-number inference.

title: A chromosome-scale genome assembly of Artemisia argyi reveals unbiased subgenome evolution and key contributions of gene duplication to volatile terpenoid diversity.
evidence_scope: A. argyi chromosome-scale genome, recent WGD, TPS expansion, germacrene/borneol/camphor pathways, and ADS loss-of-function context
decision_rationale: Primary comparative-genomics study directly informs the A. annua/A. argyi contrast; reported ADS deletion and TPS counts remain release-, ploidy-, and function-dependent until common reannotation and gene-tree reconciliation.

title: Variation in terpenoids in leaves of Artemisia annua grown under different LED spectra resulting in diverse antimalarial activities against Plasmodium falciparum.
evidence_scope: controlled LED-induced chemotype shifts and matched P. falciparum NF54 activity
decision_rationale: Primary environment-chemotype-parasite study; metabolite correlations do not identify a single causal terpene or establish clinical efficacy.

title: Polyol monoterpenes and sesquiterpene lactones from the Pacific Northwest plant Artemisia suksdorfii.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed monoterpene and sesquiterpene-lactone isolation
decision_rationale: Primary high-field NMR and X-ray isolation study expands class-balanced Artemisia chemical space; no antiparasitic endpoint or quantitative chemotype denominator.

title: Mono- and sesquiterpenes and antifungal constituents from Artemisia species.
evidence_scope: multi-species terpene isolation and antifungal assay
decision_rationale: Primary isolation study covers monoterpene, sesquiterpene-lactone, and triterpene-associated chemistry across three Artemisia taxa; fungal endpoints are retained as non-parasitic context.

title: Triterpenoids, p-coumaric acid esters and flavonoids from Artemisia igniaria.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed triterpene isolation
decision_rationale: Primary spectroscopic isolation study adds specimen-bounded C30 coverage; no antiparasitic endpoint or pathway function is inferred.

title: [Studies on sesquiterpenelactones. IX. Seasonal variation of chemical constitution of Artemisia feddei collected in Kochi prefecture].
evidence_scope: seasonal sesquiterpene-lactone chemistry
decision_rationale: Primary indexed seasonal-chemistry record strengthens phenology coverage; abstract was unavailable, so compound-level direction remains pending full-text verification.

title: Sesquiterpene Lactones and Other Constituents from Artemisia feddei.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed sesquiterpene-lactone isolation
decision_rationale: Primary abstract reports five lactones including two new guaianolides from aerial parts; no antiparasitic endpoint or abundance generalization.

title: Lignans and sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia sieversiana and Inula racemosa.
evidence_scope: structure-confirmed guaianolide isolation and antifungal context
decision_rationale: Primary abstract reports one known and three new guaianolides from A. sieversiana; antifungal testing is retained as non-parasitic context.

title: Use of high-performance liquid chromatographic peak deconvolution and peak labelling to identify antiparasitic components in plant extracts.
evidence_scope: parasite-oriented analytical identification of A. absinthium sesquiterpene lactones
decision_rationale: Primary abstract reports tentative identification of alpha-santonin and ketopelenolid-A in methanolic A. absinthium extracts; retain as an attribution lead, not proof of compound-level efficacy or target engagement.

title: [Effectiveness of the treatment of ascariasis with santonin prepared from Artemisia transiliensis].

title: Extraction of artemisinin and artemisinic acid from Artemisia annua L. using supercritical carbon dioxide.
evidence_scope: supercritical extraction and stability of artemisinin and artemisinic acid

title: Functional analysis of CYP71AV1 reveals the evolutionary landscape of artemisinin biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: A. annua CYP71AV1/GAO evolutionary reclassification and recombinant enzyme function

title: Studies on dynamics of growth and biosynthesis of artemisinin in hairy roots of Artemisia annua L.
evidence_scope: A. annua hairy-root growth and artemisinin production dynamics

title: Effect of plant density on the yields of artemisinin and essential oil in Artemisia annua cropped under low input cost management in North-Central India.
evidence_scope: A. annua field density, artemisinin yield, and essential-oil yield

title: Impact of Long-Term Copper Exposure on Growth, Photosynthesis, Antioxidant Defence System and Artemisinin Biosynthesis in Soil-Grown Artemisia annua Genotypes.

title: Exogenous hydrogen sulphide alleviates copper stress impacts in Artemisia annua L.: Growth, antioxidant metabolism, glandular trichome development and artemisinin biosynthesis.
evidence_scope: A. annua hydrogen-sulfide rescue, trichomes, and artemisinin under copper stress

evidence_scope: A. annua AaWRKY17 defense-linked ADS regulation and artemisinin

title: Profiling of phytohormone-specific microRNAs and characterization of the miR160-ARF1 module involved in glandular trichome development and artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua.
evidence_scope: A. annua miR160-ARF1 control of trichomes and artemisinin biosynthesis

title: 50th anniversary of artemisinin: From the discovery to allele-aware genome assembly of Artemisia annua
evidence_scope: allele-aware A. annua genome and artemisinin history

title: Hairy root culture of Artemisia annua L. by Ri plasmid transformation and biosynthesis of artemisinin.
evidence_scope: A. annua Ri-plasmid hairy-root production and culture-factor effects
decision_rationale: Primary transformed-root study reports artemisinin production and condition-dependent growth/output; transformed roots are not native aerial chemotypes and no parasite assay was reported.
